key_insight: Homogeneous WC–Co–Cr powder and spray process control jointly determine coating density, phase uniformity, hardness, and friction behavior.
engineering_relevance: Selecting detonation spraying or HVOF lets engineers tune wear resistance versus surface densification for machine parts operating under high load and friction.
method: Compared WC–Co–Cr coatings made by detonation spraying and HVOF.
Used SEM and EDS to examine morphology, microstructure, and phase distribution.
Assessed tribological and mechanical performance, including microhardness and friction coefficient.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that detonation spraying produced the hardest coating (about 1449 HV), while HVOF achieved a dense, uniform coating with a low friction coefficient (Kt = 0.143).
watch_item: Performance is highly sensitive to starting powder morphology and spraying conditions, so results may not transfer directly across different powder lots or process settings.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
